This interesting project developed by Jeff Halter (introduced via Daring Fireball) allows users to run original 68k After Dark screensaver modules on modern Macs. Details below.

「Run Classic After Dark Screensavers on Modern macOS」

Depending on when you started using or became interested in Macs, you may remember After Dark—a collection of screensavers that was almost a must-have for Macintosh computers in the 1990s. At the very least, you've probably heard of the famous Flying Toasters screensaver.

For years, running these classic screensavers generally required vintage hardware or a classic Mac OS emulator, and the process was quite cumbersome. However, a new project called Afterglow makes running them on modern Macs much easier.

As John Gruber mentioned on Daring Fireball, this project was developed by Jeff Halter, who previously created Lunacy—a native Swift application that lets users play the classic game Lunatic Fringe from More After Dark on modern Macs.

Afterglow runs original modules through a dedicated emulator designed specifically for After Dark modules, without needing a full classic Mac OS environment. Notably, Afterglow also comes bundled with a modern macOS screensaver module, allowing users to set any imported After Dark module as their Mac's screensaver.

Here's what Halter had to say about the philosophy behind creating this project:

In the 90s, Berkeley Systems' After Dark screensavers brought Flying Toasters, Fish, and starry night skies to every Macintosh screen. Beyond their practical purpose of preventing burn-in on CRT displays, they also provided entertainment—their animations were fun, surreal, beautiful, and sometimes even a little nauseating. They are works of art worth preserving. Running After Dark modules today often requires painstakingly setting up a Mac OS emulator or using vintage hardware. Even so, no single emulator or vintage computer can run every module perfectly: sometimes the animations are too fast, sometimes too slow. Afterglow is an emulator purpose-built for running After Dark modules—it runs the original 68k module code, not a remake or port—and doesn't rely on any ROMs or classic Mac OS. This project was created in the spirit of software preservation, so that everyone can easily enjoy After Dark today and for years to come.

The project website notes that Afterglow does not include any After Dark modules, but provides tutorials on how to find and import modules into Afterglow.

Halter also mentioned that Afterglow includes features such as module controls, full-screen mode, random playback, multi-module support, 3D cover flow appearance, CRT shaders, a resource viewer, and a DrawMorph editor.
